# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 37 (Bi-Vb Pc37)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc37
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 37
**Title (English, from literature):** Wandering within the country
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 37 (*Antoraṭṭha*, "Wandering within the country") is a disciplinary training rule in the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule stipulates that a nun who travels through a dangerous or frightening area within her own country without the company of a caravan or traveling group (*satthikā*) incurs an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [Hüsken 1997]. The text's internal word commentary defines "within the country" (*antoraṭṭhe*) as the realm of whichever ruler she resides in, and characterizes dangerous regions as those bearing signs of bandits and thieves [Hüsken 1997]. As Ute Hüsken observes, this rule—alongside the immediately following Pācittiya 38, which addresses traveling outside the country (*tiroraṭṭhe*)—was designed primarily to safeguard nuns against dangers on the road rather than to curtail their freedom of movement [Hüsken 1997].

DharmaNexus detects extensive Pali-internal text reuse, particularly with Pācittiya 38, sharing an almost identical 3,147-character sequence (§0.1–2.2.7) with a similarity score of 0.97, as well as formulaic procedural phrasing shared with Pācittiya 39, Saṅghādisesa 3, and various other Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga provisions [DharmaNexus]. Corresponding rules governing travel in dangerous areas appear across other early Vinaya lineages, including the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, and Mahāsāṃghika-Lokottaravāda traditions in Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit. Cross-language matches identified by DharmaNexus include alignments with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-3) [DharmaNexus]. An English translation of the rule and its commentary has been published by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
